references.text: Isaiah speaks of the Lord giving him a gift of speech to speak right words—this points to Jesus' gracious words that amazed the people.
The psalm describes one who is fairest among the children of men, with grace poured out upon his lips—something reflected in the people's reaction to Jesus' gracious teaching.
Also in Matthew's account of Jesus' visit to his hometown, the people are amazed at his wisdom but take offense because they know his family—paralleling the question 'Is this not Joseph's son?'
Mark's parallel account where the people in the synagogue at Nazareth are amazed at Jesus' wisdom and ask about his family background.
Already as a twelve-year-old, all were amazed at Jesus' understanding and answers—an early parallel to the people's amazement at his words in Nazareth.
Also in John's gospel, the crowd asks 'Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph?'—they know his earthly origin and therefore doubt his heavenly mission.
The servants who were sent to arrest Jesus returned and said 'No one ever spoke like this man'—a testimony to his gracious and powerful words.
Luke's genealogy identifies Jesus as the son of Joseph (as people thought), which forms the background for the people's question in the synagogue.
Joseph and Mary were amazed at what was said about the child Jesus—a pattern of amazement over Jesus' person that is repeated in Nazareth.
